result.summary: Enables clang-tidy's `readability-inconsistent-declaration-parameter-name` check and updates mismatched parameter names across declarations and definitions throughout the codebase. It also removes unused serialization overloads for `unique_ptr<const T>` and marks functions used only within their own translation units as static.
result.problem: Parameter names between function declarations in headers and definitions in source files drift apart over time, causing inconsistency and slight confusion during development.
evidence: PR description: 'Declarations and definitions tend to drift apart. We could align these, and then enforce that via clang-tidy... This may not be worth the (initial) churn / we may also be fine with inconsistency here.'
result.scope_notes: A wide-ranging mechanical refactor touching 75 files to rename parameters in declarations or definitions, combined with clang-tidy configuration updates. It is based on #36743 to avoid double-churn on functions being removed or made static.
result.card: Enforces consistent parameter naming between function declarations and definitions across the codebase by enabling clang-tidy's readability-inconsistent-declaration-parameter-name check. Parameter names in headers and implementations drift apart over time, reducing code clarity. The author opened this as an RFC, noting that the community must decide whether the initial churn across 75 files is worth the consistency benefit. Based on #36743.

risk.why: Mechanical renames of function parameters and clang-tidy configuration changes could cause build failures if a parameter name shadows an existing identifier, but cannot cause runtime harm.
